chapter: Faith, Paris life and later years
title: Keeping his religion private; the 1963 Carthage festival
summary: He never told other musicians of his conversion; Tunisians welcomed him as a brother at the first Carthage festival in 1963, but he never used his Muslim name.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well, so then, later, because after you got out of the army was like in 1946 or something like that.
Now, when different musicians around New York became converts, that was a little different, wasn't it?
I would never let them know that I had
They don't know it till today -- well, Dizzy knows, because he was --
-- he's always been close to me.
You know. So he knows. But a lot of people --
Like sometimes they'll write about it or something like that, because when I went to Tunisia, the people would always say, 'Welcome home, brother,' you know, every time I'd play Tunisia.
You know? So then the newspapers, the journalists got ahold of it.
And so that's how people know that --
Some people know that I'm a Muslim.
Because the first festival at Carthage in Tunisia, we played in the ruins of Carthage.
Who played? Who was with you?
Well, Nathan Davis, and with my group, you know.
I see. In what year was that?
It was the first concert in Carthage.
And the people knew I was a convert into Islam, so they treated me like one of them, like a brother. So that's how I went to Carthage in the first place.
And I could take whoever I wanted to take.
And we played the first festival in Tunisia. And they had a big sign like, 'Bienvenue, cher frere,' and right across the big main street.
And, "Kenny Clarke," and they didn't use my Muslim name. I never use it. Only in business and personal things, you know.
But I've been Kenny Clarke ever since. No-one knows exactly whether I'm converted, or some doubts about it.
But I never made a big thing about it.
Yeah, because it's a private thing.
I say you can touch everything except my religion.
I don't share that with anyone.
